results.summary_before: Tiny Blackjack is a simplified Blackjack game implemented entirely in digital hardware, with game logic as a finite-state machine and a 16-bit LFSR for pseudo-random card generation. The design fits into a single TinyTapeout tile and includes features like doubling down and real-time hand total calculation. It is tested by playing the game using buttons and observing the output. It is notable for implementing a complete game in a small footprint.
results.summary: This project is an 8-bit CPU implemented in Verilog on a single Tiny Tapeout tile. It performs instructions such as arithmetic and load operations and outputs the result of each instruction on the eight output pins. A test script simulates the instruction register, allowing custom assembly programs to be loaded and tested. The design is a work in progress with features to be added as time and complexity allow.

results.summary_before: This is an analog phase-locked loop targeting a 2.4 GHz output, including a bandgap reference for the charge pump. The design uses a VCO and charge pump to generate a high-frequency clock signal. It is implemented at the transistor level and is intended for RF applications. The design is notable for its analog implementation of a frequency synthesizer.
results.summary: This project is a VGA metaballs graphics demo written in Verilog on a single Tiny Tapeout tile. It follows a failed attempt at metaballs in the first demo competition and aims to reset the ball positions correctly this time. It works like other VGA projects and produces no sound. It requires a VGA PMOD connected to the output pins.

results.summary_before: This project is a digital circuit that implements a pseudo-random number generator using a linear feedback shift register (LFSR). It produces a sequence of pseudo-random bits based on a seed value. The design is intended for use in games or other applications requiring random numbers. It is notable for its simple and efficient LFSR-based implementation.
results.summary: Journey is a two-tile intro featuring dark tunnels and a cat on a red balloon casting spells, with chiptune music and a scrolling text overlay. It is written in SystemVerilog and outputs 640x480 VGA at 60 Hz plus 1-bit sigma-delta audio on uio[7]. The demo starts automatically after reset when a 25 MHz clock is applied. It requires a Tiny VGA Pmod and a TT Audio Pmod.

results.summary: Orion Iron Ion is a two-tile demo originally created for the TT10 demo competition. It is written in Verilog and outputs VGA video plus audio on uio[7], with two advance inputs on ui[6] and ui[7]. The demo starts directly after reset, and setting all inputs to zero gives the default behavior. It requires a TinyVGA Pmod and Mike's audio Pmod.
